body:
Topic picked from https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2996#issuecomment-2819901941

Documented security decision requirement:
| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **7.1.1** | Verify that the user's session inactivity period and maximum session lifetime before re-authentication are documented, appropriate in combination with other controls, and that documentation includes justification for any deviations from NIST SP 800-63B re-authentication requirements. | 2 | v5.0.be-1.3.1 |

Implementation requirements:
| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **7.3.1** | Verify that there is an inactivity timeout such that re-authentication is enforced according to risk analysis and documented security decisions. | 2 | v5.0.be-3.3.5 |
| **7.3.2** | Verify that there is an absolute maximum session lifetime such that re-authentication is enforced according to risk analysis and documented security decisions. | 2 | v5.0.be-3.3.2 |

In [the Glossary](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x90-Appendix-A_Glossary.md):

* Absolute Maximum Session Lifetime - Also referred to as "Overall Timeout" by NIST, this is the maximal amount of time a session can remain active following authentication regardless of user interaction. This is a component of session expiration.
* Inactivity Timeout - This is the length of time a session can remain active in the absence of user interaction with the application. This is a component of session expiration.

---

As implementation requirements use the same terminology as written in the Glossary, then the most logical fix is to update the wording for 7.1.1.

ping @ryarmst
title: Sync session terminology for inactivity timeout and absolute maximum session lifetime
